clue.text: Swan runs away initially, seeing snake

parts.note: a cob is a male swan

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sees a swan bolting and then spots a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'runs away', R and A, to follow COB.
explanation.definitionFit: The cobra is a venomous hooded serpent, a familiar example of a snake.

clue.text: Clients redesigned card with a holed pattern

indicators.note: something redesigned has been put together in a new arrangement, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Customers have reworked a piece of card cut with a pattern of holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a sheet, often card, with cut-out shapes through which paint is applied.

clue.text: One who serves Tom and two queens

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
ER (Elizabeth Regina) stands for a queen; two queens give it twice

explanation.surface: A waiter or courtier attends to a man named Tom and a pair of queens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two queens' supplies ER twice; ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies and serves food and drink at events, so is literally one who serves.

clue.text: Horse beginning to mosey off round capital of Nebraska

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
the letters for off go round the next piece

parts.note: something off is out, as a light switched off

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its initial letter

explanation.surface: A horse sets off at a gentle pace around the capital city of Nebraska.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of Nebraska' is not Lincoln here; it is just the letter N, which sits inside OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mount is the horse or other animal a rider sits on.

clue.text: Quite fairly, over-embellished

parts.note: pretty can mean quite, as in pretty good
pretty can also mean fairly, as in pretty sure

explanation.surface: Something is described as rather overdone in its decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty-pretty is a disparaging term for something fussily or excessively decorated.

clue.text: Quarrel during light meal

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel
in can mean during, as in in the morning

explanation.surface: A couple squabble over a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: TIFFIN is the Anglo-Indian word for a light lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin, from British India, is a light midday meal or snack.

clue.text: Boring race rehearsal

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
a run is a race, as in a fun run

explanation.surface: A dull practice session ahead of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry run is a practice or trial performance before the real thing.

clue.text: German turned around to reveal knickers, perhaps?

indicators.note: around means the letters are scattered about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A German man spins round to show off his knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder: GERMAN TURNED, mixed up by 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are one example of underwear, an item worn beneath outer clothes; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: River runs into temporary home

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tent is a shelter used for a short time
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A river floods into a campsite tent.
explanation.walkthrough: The TRENT is a major river in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trent is one of England's longest rivers, flowing through Nottingham.

clue.text: Ballroom dance seen, opt out!

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered, put out of place

explanation.surface: Someone sees a ballroom dance being performed and decides to opt out.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step is a quick ballroom dance in duple time popular in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Someone held label in stockings

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: hose are stockings or tights
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A captive has a price label stuck in their stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held captive as security for demands being met.

clue.text: Finely chop last of cedar in outhouse

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the outbuilding

parts.note: a shed is an outbuilding

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone chops cedar wood into small pieces inside a garden outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: To shred is to cut or tear into thin strips, much as finely chopping vegetables.

clue.text: Raise and then tilt upward pilot's seat?

parts.note: to cock is to raise or tilt up, as in cocking an eyebrow

indicators.note: in a down clue, upward means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tip is to tilt

explanation.surface: Instructions for adjusting a pilot's chair: lift it and angle it up.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockpit is the compartment where a pilot sits; the question mark notes it is more than a seat.

clue.text: Clumsy person playing with fire gets burnt

indicators.note: playing with the following letters means rearranging them freely

explanation.surface: A clumsy person who plays with fire ends up burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'play with fire and you get burnt' hides the anagram: 'playing with' signals it, and FIRE GETS BURNT is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A butterfingers is someone who keeps dropping things, a clumsy person.

clue.text: Bombing risk I rate absurd

indicators.note: absurd suggests the letters are in a nonsensical order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone judges a bombing risk to be ridiculously high or low.
explanation.definitionFit: An air strike is an attack by aircraft, typically dropping bombs.

clue.text: Turn of phrase for angel

indicators.note: a turn of the word means its letters are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer looks for a turn of phrase to describe an angel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn of phrase' reads as an idiom for an expression, but 'Turn of' signals the anagram of PHRASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is one of the highest order of angels in Christian tradition.

clue.text: Tree some hazel, maybe

indicators.note: some says only a part of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: A tree that is perhaps a hazel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hazel' looks like the tree being defined, but the answer is drawn from 'hazEL Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: The elm is a large deciduous tree with serrated leaves.

clue.text: Tenerife court dealt with forger

indicators.note: dealt with suggests the letters are handled and dealt out like cards into a new order

explanation.surface: A court on Tenerife tried and sentenced a forger.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterfeiter makes fake money or goods, which is to say a forger.

clue.text: Reportedly, stolen property in minstrel's possession?

indicators.note: reportedly says the answer sounds like the word for the clue's stolen goods

parts.note: loot is stolen goods

explanation.surface: A wandering singer is said to be holding stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval minstrel typically carried and played a plucked stringed instrument like this.

clue.text: Perfect or else imperfect around banks of river heading south

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the next piece
imperfect suggests the letters are spoilt and need rearranging
the banks of a river are its two outer edges, so its first and last letters
heading means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A perfect or else flawed stretch of river running south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imperfect' turns OR ELSE into EORLES; 'around' puts it around RR (outer letters of 'river'); 'heading south' adds S at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without mistakes or flaws is perfect, an exact synonym.

clue.text: No record in little jotter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the record inside the word for little

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone finds no record written in a small notebook.
explanation.definitionFit: A jotter is a small pad for quick notes, the same thing under another name.

clue.text: Disregard poor region

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in bad shape and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A deprived area is being neglected by the authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to pay it no attention, to disregard it.

clue.text: Part of Connecticut, a hospitable US state

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A welcoming region of Connecticut is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Connecticut' looks like the state wanted, but the answer runs through 'ConnecticUT A Hospitable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of the USA, home of Salt Lake City.

clue.text: Reading out letter, Earl Grey, say?

indicators.note: reading out says the answer is how the letter's name is spoken

parts.note: the letter T is spelt and named tee

explanation.surface: Someone reads a letter aloud over a cup of Earl Grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earl Grey' looks like a nobleman, but it is a blend of tea flavoured with bergamot.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Grey is a well-known black blend flavoured with bergamot oil, an example of the drink.
